content:
We got several templates. The first reaction_id 87121 seems to involve Br-CH2-... and NH2-CH2-... Not exactly our case. But we can pick a template that does N-alkylation of heteroaryl with benzyl bromide. For simplicity, we can use reaction_id 378298 (template for N-alkylation). Let's inspect its retro_smarts_template: It shows [C:6]-[N;H0;D3;+0:7](-[C:8])-[CH2;D2;+0:4]-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[c:2]):[cH;D2;+0:3]:[c:5]>>Br-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[c:2]):[c;H0;D3;+0:3](-[CH3;D1;+0:4]):[c:5].[C:6]-[NH;D2;+0:7]-[C:8]

Seems to be alkylation of heteroaryl nitrogen with benzyl bromide (aryl bromide). Good.

Thus we can use template_id 378298 for N-alkylation step.

Now we need template for amide formation: we have reaction_id 881195 and 208284. Choose 208284 (simpler). Use template_id 208284.

Now we need leaves: For amide step, reactants: 4-methoxyaniline (COc1ccc(N)cc1) and triazine carboxylic acid (or acid chloride). The template likely expects amine and acid (or acid chloride). The retro_smarts_template shows [#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](-[C:4])=[O;H0;D1;+0:1]>>C-C-C-n1... Actually it's a retro template for amide formation? The product side is amide, reactants side is amine and acid? The retro_smarts_template shows amide product on left? Let's not worry.

We can assume template works.

Now we need the triazine carboxylic acid precursor: It is the triazine core after N-alkylation (i.e., after step 2). So after N-alkylation, we have triazine with side chain attached and a carboxylic acid group (or maybe amide carbonyl). The target after N-alkylation is the same as target but without the aniline amide (i.e., the acid). So we need to define that intermediate SMILES.

Let's construct intermediate: The target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

Remove the amide: replace NC(=O) with COOH? Actually the amide carbonyl attached to triazine carbon. So the acid would be COc1cccc(C(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1? Wait the amide nitrogen is attached to anisidine. So acid would be COc1cccc(C(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1 (i.e., anisidine replaced by H). But the anisidine part is the aromatic ring with methoxy and attached to carbonyl directly (aryl carbonyl). Actually the amide is anilide: anisidine nitrogen attached to carbonyl. So the acid would be COc1cccc(C(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1 (i.e., anisidine ring with carbonyl attached directly to ring? Wait the carbonyl is attached to the triazine carbon, not to the anisidine ring. The anisidine is attached via nitrogen to carbonyl. So the acid would be COc1cccc(C(=O)N?) No.

Better: The amide bond is between aniline N and carbonyl carbon attached to triazine. So the acid component is the triazine carbonyl (i.e., triazine-COOH). So the acid SMILES: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N C(=O)O? Actually carbonyl attached to triazine carbon, with OH instead of N-aniline. So acid SMILES: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N C(=O)O . Need to attach to the same carbon as in target. So acid SMILES: O=C(O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N

Thus the acid is O=C(O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N

Now the N-alkylation step: starting from triazine core with N-H (i.e., O=C(O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N? Wait the side chain is attached to triazine N via Cc3... That's already present. Actually the side chain is attached to triazine N via Cc3... So the N-alkylation attaches the benzyl group to the triazine N. So the precursor before N-alkylation would be O=C(O)c2nnn(c2)N? Actually the triazine N is unsubstituted (NH). The side chain is attached via N-alkylation later. So the precursor is O=C(O)c2nnn(c2)N (i.e., 2-aminotriazine-5-carboxylic acid). Let's define SMILES: O=C(O)c1nnn(c1)N

Check: c1nnn(c1)N is a triazine with N at position? Might be okay.

Thus step 2: N-alkylation of O=C(O)c1nnn(c1)N with benzyl bromide (bearing phenyl with azetidine substituent). The product is O=C(O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N (the acid with side chain). Good.

Now step 3: amide coupling with 4-methoxyaniline to give target.

Thus leaves: 4-methoxyaniline (COc1ccc(N)cc1), 2-aminotriazine-5-carboxylic acid (O=C(O)c1nnn(c1)N), benzyl bromide with phenyl-azetidine substituent (BrCc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3). Need SMILES for that benzyl bromide: BrCc1ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc1

SMILES: BrCc1ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc1

Now check if these leaves are commercially available. Use is_buyable.
